easy.explanation: Malachi 3:1 says, “Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.”
easy.q: Whom does the LORD say He will send to prepare the way before Him?

answers: A refiner’s fire and fullers’ soap
easy.explanation: Malachi 3:2 compares Him to “a refiner’s fire, and like fullers’ sope.”
easy.q: What is the Lord compared to in the work of purification?

easy.explanation: Malachi 3:3 says, “he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver.”
easy.q: Whom will the Lord purify and purge?

answers: They will offer unto the LORD an offering in righteousness
They will cease serving in the Temple
They will crown a new king
medium.explanation: The purification will enable them to offer an offering in righteousness.
medium.q: What will be the result of the purification of the sons of Levi?

answers: Who can endure or remain firm
medium.explanation: The question asks who can endure the Lord’s appearing and judgment.
medium.q: In the question, “who shall stand when he appeareth?”, what does “stand” mean?

answers: Sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, and oppressors
medium.explanation: Malachi 3:5 lists several sinners, including sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, and oppressors.
medium.q: Against whom does the LORD say He will come near to judgment?

answers: Purification makes their offering acceptable and righteous
The offering itself purifies the sons of Levi
challenge.explanation: After being purified, the sons of Levi can offer unto the LORD an offering in righteousness.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between purifying the sons of Levi and their offering?

answers: That the LORD changes His laws
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the LORD’s constancy and unchanging nature.
challenge.q: What does the statement “For I am the LORD, I change not” emphasize?

answers: Because the LORD does not change
Because nothing is required of them
Because they have all already been punished
challenge.explanation: Malachi connects their preservation with the LORD’s unchanging character.
challenge.q: Why are the sons of Jacob not consumed?

paragraphs.title: Returning to God and the Tithes

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “Return unto me, and I will return unto you.”
easy.q: To whom is the people called to return?

easy.explanation: The people are accused of robbing God “in tithes and offerings.”
easy.q: In what did the people rob God?

easy.explanation: Malachi 3:10 says, “Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse.”
easy.q: Where were the people commanded to bring all the tithes?

medium.explanation: The LORD promises to open the windows of heaven and pour out a blessing.
medium.q: What does the LORD promise if the people bring the tithes properly?

answers: They are under judgment because of their disobedience
They are under a special blessing
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the judgment resulting from robbing God in tithes and offerings.
medium.q: What does “cursed with a curse” mean in this passage?

answers: The devourer will not destroy the fruits of the ground
medium.explanation: The LORD says He will rebuke the devourer so that it will not destroy the fruits of the ground.
medium.q: What protection does the LORD promise for the crops?

answers: The nations will call Israel blessed
The nations will bring the tithes instead
The nations will forbid worship of the LORD
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises that all nations shall call them blessed when the land becomes a delightsome land.
challenge.q: What connection is made between bringing tithes and the nations’ response?

answers: Robbery through neglected tithes, a call to bring them, and a promise of blessing
Blessing, rebellion, and the abolition of tithes
Judgment, war, and the rebuilding of the Temple
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the charge of robbing God to the command to bring tithes and the promise of blessing.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the passage?

answers: The people immediately confess their sin
The people do not understand what they have done wrong
The people have already brought every tithe
challenge.explanation: The people ask what they must change, even though the LORD identifies their neglect of tithes and offerings.
challenge.q: What does the question “Wherein shall we return?” reveal?

paragraphs.title: The Complaints of the Wicked and the Faithfulness of God-Fearers

answers: It is vain to serve God
easy.explanation: They say, “It is vain to serve God,” and ask what profit comes from keeping His ordinance.
easy.q: What complaint do the people make?

easy.explanation: Malachi says, “Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another.”
easy.q: Who spoke often with one another?

easy.explanation: A book of remembrance was written for those who feared the LORD and thought upon His name.
easy.q: What was written before the LORD?

answers: The proud were called happy, and wicked people seemed to prosper
medium.explanation: The people observed that the proud were called happy and that those who worked wickedness were set up.
medium.q: Why did the wicked appear successful to the complainers?

answers: They served with sorrow and complained that it brought no profit
They walked joyfully in a procession
They traveled quickly to the Temple
medium.explanation: The phrase describes their sorrowful religious observance, which they claimed had brought them no benefit.
medium.q: What does “we have walked mournfully before the LORD” mean?

answers: They spoke and encouraged one another
medium.explanation: They spoke often one to another, and the LORD heard them.
medium.q: What did those who feared the LORD do when others complained?

answers: The complainers focused on earthly profit, while the faithful thought upon God’s name
The complainers brought tithes, while the faithful refused to serve
The complainers were Levites, while the faithful were foreigners
challenge.explanation: The complainers judged service by apparent profit, while the faithful remained mindful of the LORD’s name.
challenge.q: What is the main difference between the complainers and those who feared the LORD?

answers: The words and faithfulness of God-fearers are remembered before Him
Only the names of the wicked are recorded
challenge.explanation: The book is written for those who feared the LORD and thought upon His name.
challenge.q: What does the book of remembrance signify in this passage?

answers: The LORD will spare and distinguish those who serve Him
The wicked will receive the promised reward
challenge.explanation: The LORD promises to spare His faithful servants as a man spares his own son.
challenge.q: What future event is suggested by the phrase “in that day when I make up my jewels”?

paragraphs.title: The Day of Judgment: Destruction for the Wicked and Salvation for the Faithful

easy.explanation: Malachi 4:1 says, “Behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven.”
easy.q: What will the coming day be like for the wicked?

easy.explanation: The passage says the proud and those who do wickedly shall be stubble.
easy.q: What will the wicked be like on that day?

easy.explanation: The promise is, “But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise.”
easy.q: What will arise for those who fear the LORD’s name?

answers: They will be burned so that neither root nor branch remains
medium.explanation: The coming day will burn them up and leave them without root or branch.
medium.q: What will happen to the wicked according to the description of the day?

medium.explanation: The Sun of righteousness rises with healing, and they will go forth and grow up like calves of the stall.
medium.q: What does the salvation of those who fear God include?

medium.explanation: The expression describes the healing and restoration brought to those who fear the LORD.
medium.q: What does “healing in his wings” mean?

answers: The wicked are burned like stubble, while the faithful receive light and healing
The wicked receive blessing, while the faithful become stubble
Both groups receive the same fate
challenge.explanation: The passage presents a sharp contrast between destruction for the wicked and healing joy for the faithful.
challenge.q: How does the passage contrast the fate of the wicked with that of those who fear God?

challenge.explanation: The image describes them going forth freely and joyfully after the Sun of righteousness rises.
challenge.q: What does the image of calves from the stall suggest about the faithful?

answers: Their destruction will be complete, with no lasting continuation
They will begin to flourish again
challenge.explanation: Root and branch represent continued life and growth; neither will remain for the wicked.
challenge.q: What does it mean that the wicked will have neither root nor branch?

paragraphs.title: Remembering the Torah and the Message of Elijah

answers: The law of the sons of Levi
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Remember ye the law of Moses my servant.”
easy.q: Whose law are the people commanded to remember?

easy.explanation: The LORD promises, “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet.”
easy.q: Whom will the LORD send before the coming of the great and dreadful day?

easy.explanation: Elijah will turn the heart of the fathers to the children and the heart of the children to their fathers.
easy.q: Between whom will Elijah turn the hearts?

answers: After the day of the LORD
Before the great and dreadful day of the LORD
medium.explanation: Elijah is promised before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.
The final warning describes judgment if the hearts of the generations are not turned.
medium.q: What does “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse” warn about?

answers: To turn the hearts of fathers and children toward one another
To purify the Levites with fire
medium.explanation: His role is described as turning the hearts of fathers to children and children to fathers.
medium.q: What is Elijah’s role according to the passage?

answers: Both prepare the people for the future and the day of the LORD
Remembering the law cancels Elijah’s mission
Elijah is sent to replace the law of Moses
challenge.explanation: The book ends with a call to remember the law and a promise of Elijah before the day of the LORD.
challenge.q: How are remembering Moses’ law and Elijah’s message related?

answers: There can be reconciliation and restored relationships between generations
The relationship between parents and children will be broken
challenge.explanation: Turning hearts toward one another points to reconciliation, repentance, and restored relationships.
challenge.q: What message of comfort is found in Elijah’s mission?

answers: The LORD may smite the earth with a curse
The land will be filled with blessing
challenge.explanation: The passage concludes with the warning that the LORD may smite the earth with a curse.
challenge.q: What may happen if the hearts of the generations are not turned?
